summary.intent: Bootstrap release-please versioning for the cipher-box project by aligning api-client versions with the API, creating missing tags to fix an excessive changelog on PR #427, and validating the release system with a quick task (expose API version on /health endpoint).
summary.outcome: Successfully aligned api-client versions (0.33.0/0.4.0 → 0.35.0), fixed OpenAPI version to be dynamic from package.json, created 6 missing bootstrap tags, resolved PR review comments, and implemented the /health version field including the OpenAPI spec — confirming the release-please pipeline works end-to-end.

repo: release-please treats entire commit history as unreleased when no prior tags exist, causing massive changelogs — bootstrap tags must be created before first run

HealthController is excluded from the NestJS OpenApiGeneratorModule because it depends on TypeOrmHealthIndicator which requires a real DB connection; the health endpoint spec is manually defined in apps/api/scripts/generate-openapi.ts around line 237-264

Phase 41 discussion log (41-DISCUSSION-LOG.md line 106) specified monotonic major.minor versioning for web and desktop apps, but implementation defaulted to semver — decision was deferred as acceptable for now
The api-client and crates/api-client versions should track the API version (apps/api) since they are tightly coupled
fix: commit prefix triggers a patch version bump in release-please; use chore(ci): for tooling/CI changes that should not bump versions
pnpm api:generate output formatting can change (compact vs expanded JSON arrays) based on how swagger serializes, producing whitespace-only diffs in openapi.json

code.finding: OpenAPI version was hardcoded as '0.1.0'; changed to read from process.env.npm_package_version with package.json fallback
Same hardcoded '0.1.0' version; changed to fail-fast if npm_package_version env var is missing
Health endpoint is manually defined here (not auto-generated) — new fields added to the controller must also be manually added to this spec definition
openapi.json added as extra-file with jsonpath ($['info']['version']) so release-please bumps the nested JSON version field automatically on API releases

workflow: When squashing commits to change a commit message (e.g. fix: → chore(ci):), soft reset + recommit + force push is the clean approach; interactive rebase can leave a detached HEAD in complex situations
Bootstrap tags for release-please should be created at the commit just before the release tooling was introduced, not at HEAD
CodeRabbit and GitHub Copilot both flagged process.env.npm_package_version as unreliable without a fallback — the correct pattern is to read package.json directly as a fallback
The GSD quick workflow executor can be bypassed in favor of direct implementation when the user has specific requirements (like commit message scope) that the executor won't honor by default

friction: Cargo.lock regeneration pulled in unrelated dependency updates when bumping crate version — required manual targeted update with cargo update -p instead
Auto-merge on PR #428 appeared enabled (user said 'auto merge is on') but gh pr view showed autoMergeRequest as null — caused confusion and delay
The GSD executor agent was interrupted mid-flight because it wouldn't use the user-specified feat(api): commit scope — had to execute the task manually
git merge origin main was run instead of git merge origin/main (space instead of slash) but still worked via ort strategy, creating an unnecessary merge commit on the feature branch
open_items: 15 bootstrap tags were needed but only 6 were missing — need to verify all package tags are correctly anchored before next release-please run
Monotonic major.minor versioning for web and desktop apps (per phase 41 discussion) was deferred — currently using semver for all packages
The /health endpoint version field was added to the controller and OpenAPI spec but the api-client generated types should be verified to include the version property in the HealthResponse model
openapi.json formatting churn (compact vs expanded arrays) from api:generate produces noisy diffs — worth investigating if orval/swagger serialization can be stabilized
